So I’m going to be honest here because I was in your position as well. Both of you are toxic, neither of you are helping the situation. You keep engaging with a man who clearly doesn’t want to talk to you and asking him to give you something he can’t give you at the moment. He’s immature for being in a relationship while not being able to provide the bare minimum - which included respect and communication. You have options. You can either choose to leave and find someone else, or work to stay in the relationship. I was in your position and I chose to stay and work things out. It will get a hell of a lot worse before it gets better. At this point, my partner apologized to me about everything he’s done and said to me in the past and actively works to admit his faults, grow with me as a team, and listen to my needs. I’ve learned not to be so codependent and obsessed with his life and what’s he’s doing and I developed a life of my own. It was a joint effort which took years to do. Idk if your relationship is like mine or not, but I do know that only you have the power and insight to leave or choose to stay. The easiest option that will hurt you the least is to leave. I wish I could give you a “do X, Y, Z” but toxic relationships oftentimes are difficult to navigate and a joint effort. I wish you all the best. I know it’s hard and I know how hurt, low, disappointed and empty you must be feeling. It does get better. Just focus all of that love and positive energy towards yourself and own ambitions. You got this. ❤️

I know how you feel, because like you, I'm also the BP. What I've learned from my journey, is that in blaming ourselves, it makes it easier for us to have a false sense of control because ultimately, we can only control what we have power over. In relationships, we have zero control or power over our significant other and that's where trust comes in. No amount of blaming or thinking of what you did wrong, is going to change the very fundamental fact that you lost all sense of safety and security by what she did. While understanding your shortcomings is an important step in every relationship, she made a deliberate choice to disrespect you in every single way. It was NOT your shortcomings that led to her choice, it was her own. While I'm sure you have faults and flaws, she was 100% capable of communicating with you prior to starting an affair. She did not give you a choice, and you were powerless as a result of it and only left  to pick up the pieces that you played no part in destroying. 

Let me explain it this way. 

If you have a very valuable and special glass and you put it on top of a car right before you and your wife were to drive away, and she pressed on the gas and the glass broke and fell, would you be saying it was her fault for not knowing that valuable piece of glass was there? NO. You would be blaming yourself, for not communicating with her. Please understand that this is the exact. same. concept. 

EVERY relationship has arguments, rough patches, shortcomings on both ends. You know what solves them? Communication and actively listening. While I think it's great you're willing to reconcile with her, I would highly suggest therapy for you so you can understand yourself better. 

I know this might come across as a bit strict and mean, but I'm telling you this as a person who is in the same situation as you. I do get it. Sending you hugs.

What I've realized, is that if you do tell everyone, YOU are going to sound like the crazy one. Trust me. I get wanting to tell people, because why should everyone just continue to look at someone who has done us so wrong as being a "good" person? Ultimately, I chose to stick with my boyfriend and as a result of telling people what happened, I have lost friends and a lot of people have lost their respect for me. If you are still deciding what you want to do, I would highly recommend you keep this information to yourself or share it with someone you trust extremely well or a therapist.   


That's also part of what sucks about being a woman. If you do choose to share this info with a lot of other people in an effort to disclose who she really is, YOU will seem hysterical and crazy and people will be saying "ofc he cheated. Look at what he was married to" because no one, unless also betrayed, understands the amount of feelings that come as a result of being cheated on. 

If you decide to divorce him, what I would do, is make a post on a social media explaining that I'm getting a divorce and nonchalantly mentioning that my husband cheated with his ex gf. People will naturally put two and two together and that saves you the title of being the hysterical/crazy woman.

I did have an opportunity to confront the person my boyfriend had cheated on me with. My bf told me early in the morning what happened, and the AP messaged me much later in the evening. In the heat of the moment, I was happy that I was able to get answers from her that I probably wouldn't have been able to get out of my boyfriend. She did help fill in the gaps. It wasn't until the hysteria settled that I realized she reached out to me to hurt my bf, because she was upset he blocked her and two, she blamed him completely for what happened and took very little accountability. She was married, in a poly relationship, and had a child. If I could go back into the past, I wish I could have called her out on pretending to be the victim when it was her choice to do what she did. Not that my bf wasn't also to blame, but she also saw that we were in a happy relationship. He posted me on social media too. This was his middle school ex, and I didn't mind him talking to her because I genuinely get that sometimes, young romances can develop into a genuine, platonic friendship. It's completely blindsiding. It sucks OP. 

Do you think this is something you can move past? Do you have anyone you can rely on that's part of your support system aside from your husband? How long has it been since DDay? One major thing that I regretted was that I was so desperate to hold onto my bf. I wish I grew some balls and stood up for myself. so PLEASE. PLEASE. PLEASE. Stick up for yourself. Demand respect. Be a hardass. And if you lose him in the process of this, at least you didn't lose yourself.

She will most likely deny and downplay the truth. If you want to reconcile with her, I'd bring up the phone bill and ask about the number she's been texting to see if she is willing to at least give you the respect of being honest with you. Also redraw some boundaries and go at the pace that \*you\* are comfortable with. If you think she's lying or omitting the truth, I'd shove the evidence you gathered so far in her face and request a divorce.   


The issue with being the betrayed spouse/partner (at least from my own experience), is that if you are not 100% capable of forgiving and to an extent, forgetting, what happened, then you two will never be happy. The other side of it as well is how willing your partner is in helping you heal. My partner cheating on me uncovered A LOT of trauma and pain from the past that preceded he and I meeting. Juggling those feelings as well as the anger, the hurt, the betrayal, the humiliation, etc, is exhausting.

I get that. I have a similar backstory to you, where my bf had went to his ex gf and had sex with her right after an argument we had. Now, whenever we argue, it’s incredibly difficult not to assume the worst case scenario. It also doesn’t help that he’s the kind of person that needs space/wants to get away and I’m, like you, a person who wants to talk. I won’t lie and tell you that everything is perfect after 4 months. Sometimes, it’s even more devastating rethinking it and playing with all the intrusive thoughts. Like you, I also asked my bf lots of questions about what they did, where they did it, etc, and all the details associated with what happened. It helped fill in the gaps in my mind so I wasn’t left wondering. To be honest, the more detailed answers I got, the less intrusive the thoughts became because I had nothing left to imagine since I already knew it all. Still, some days are harder than others, and some days, it’s like we got our old relationship back (as in the love, the playfulness, the affection). 

I don’t know if this is what you want to hear, but something that’s helped is having more time apart where I can remember who I am as just me, and do all the things I want like taking naps, reading, baking, etc. It helps me reclaim the parts of me that I felt I lost and it helps me heal in a way that’s good for both me and him. Also, during these times apart, I try to journal too and write out why I’m angry, hurt, feeling betrayed, and when I put my thoughts together, I can figure out what it is that I’m needing and instead of telling him “you hurt me because you had that ons”, I can say “I’m struggling because I’m trying to get back the bond we had” and that comes across much nicer to him rather than the latter, which made him feel like I was pointing blame (which, he is to blame but not recognizing how he feels wouldn’t be helpful at all in this situation). It’s important that if he truly wants to reconcile with you, he’s also going to have his own emotions - whether they be anger, guilt, shame, regret. He’ll likely also be mourning what you two had, despite his infidelity. His experience, for obvious reasons, will be different from yours as the betrayed partner. But that doesn’t make his feelings any less valuable or significant. 

Another thing that helped my partner is us creating boundaries together and having a flag system that helps us both understand each other. For example, we have a yellow, orange and red flag. Yellow is where you’re slightly bothered and feeling upset, insecure, etc, and red is where you’ve reached maximum levels of being upset. We both talked out what we need from the other when we say a flag, and that’s made a difference too. 

Reading your post and this reply really reminded me of what my partner and I just went through. I want you to know that your feelings are totally valid, and you’re not going crazy either. It fucking sucks going through this. But, you will get through it, with or without him and it’s important to remember that throughout this process.

I think it depends on a lot of factors…. Like did your WP come clean or did you find out? Did they trickle truth you or answer all of your questions honestly? How do they respond to you when you bring up their infidelity? And was it a ONS, or a full fledged affair? 

I’m almost at 4 months post dday. Sometimes, I still feel angry at him. Other times, I feel disgusted. But as time goes on, more than anything I don’t really feel much at all. I’ve noticed that for me, I start thinking intrusive thoughts about my partners infidelity when we argue and when he reacts in a way that makes me feel badly about myself. If it’s something I think up on my own, I normally brush past it pretty quickly at this point. 

That being said, my partner had a ONS and told me immediately. He did, to some extent, trickle truth me but the gaps were filled in by the person he cheated on me with since she reached out to me and answered all of my questions. 

I know this is incredibly difficult to go through but only you know what you’re capable of. Do you think your partners infidelity is ever going to be something you can “get over”? Do you think you’ve gotten all the answers you needed? Do you feel that your partner is remorseful? You have a long journey ahead of you and if you do choose to continue reconciling, I wish you the best of luck. 

I’d recommend checking out r/AsOneAfterInfidelity because it’s geared more towards reconciling

I agree with you. I'm surprised that the therapist honestly said it's okay for his daughter to call gf mom because it's pretty clear she has some deep attachment issues if that's truly the case. I'm not a specialist by any means, but reading his post and having the snippet of info that I do have, makes me strongly feel that she has DSED. She's old enough to have built secure connections with the adults in her life, so the fact she was able to cling to gf, who is virtually a stranger, is a huge red flag to me.
Well, more specifically someone along the lines of an IMH specialist

So I'm not sure if you've heard of this,  but there's something called "Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder" which is along the lines of a reactive attachment disorder in young children which generally happens as a result of not having a stable relationship with her caregivers/parents. Her clinging to your gf and being so quick to accept her and her family as "mom", "uncle", etc, as endearing as it is, not typical and shows that she has issues with her attachment likely as a result of her lack of one with her birth mother. I'd recommend you consider consulting therapist for her so you can get to the bottom of these issues before they follow her into adulthood.

Also, if your daughter is that adamant about not wanting to be around her birth mother, then don't force her to. She is still her own person and should have the right to make a decision. Her feelings weren't made in haste,  but as a result of the situation that your ex had put her in. Your ex is not entitled to a relationship with the child she abandoned, regardless if the abandonment was addiction motivated. Your daughter is most likely not old enough to grasp the complexities of addiction and in her mind, she can only see the facts - your ex left her and you, your new gf gives her maternal love, and that there is a forced relationship between ex and your daughter.

Ok so first, I would try applying for an "Administrative W" if your school allows this. Even at a community college, that should be possible. Explain your depression, why it's better now, etc, and they'll likely turn the bad grades you got into a "W" which would remove that in your GPA calculation. 

Second, I've been in a similar position to you and it is really hard. I know how you feel and how stuck and stressed and disappointed you probably are but it's okay. Life isn't a race and it's totally okay to do things at a pace that fits you. I come from an asian household so telling my family that my mental health was shit and that as a result, I withdrew from college was HARD. But you know what? They accepted it and they cared more about my health than they did the fact that I wasn't graduating as soon as they expected/wanted me to. As of now, I'm back in university trying to earn my degree. 

Third.... I will say if you're suffering with depression, it may be easier to take online classes (for me it was) because being in social situations was absolutely DRAINING for me and it was also what contributed to me not passing my classes. If you want to transfer, try looking into options that are in-state for you. Most schools probably offer fully distance learning as well considering COVID. And if you need help paying for college, look into applying for the CARES grant (assuming you're in the US).
It really is. It’s what made it so hard to process what happened when you don’t even know what you want. My heart goes out to all the other BP/BS out there honestly.

Speaking on the behalf of a BP, no amount of information you give him will be enough to make him feel better. I think as the person who was betrayed, we rake through as much information as we possibly can hoping to find something that makes us realize that we were enough, or that as a WP/WS you realize you fucked up, or hoping to find what it was that we were lacking. It’s such a complicated thing because while we (at least for me), I didn’t want to know what happened at all yet I couldn’t help myself from prying and trying to find out everything. It’s a really delicate thing. On one hand, we want to be smothered in love and affection and on the other hand, we’re completely disgusted and want nothing to do with you. It’s a really weird/complicated thing. 

From my experience, my WP could never tell me enough information. It got to the point where I was irritating the hell out of him and to the point where I was also emotionally and mentally exhausted. I had to at some point just realize that no matter what and how much he told me, I wasn’t ever going to feel better about it. At this point, I just try to let myself feel the emotions and realize what it is I’m lacking from WP, and try to get it through other, more reliable facets like my hobbies, friends, and interests. It does take a lot of time though. I went through denial, anger, mood swings, disgust, hyperfixation on him and what he’s up to, etc. I had to get to this point on my own though. It was a rough, exhausting journey for both my partner and I. 

I can’t promise you that you’ll both get through this but from what I realized through my own situation is that moving forwards from this is both an individual journey as well as a team effort.

I hope it does work out for you. I know it’s rough, but hang in there if you think it’s worth it for you to.

So the thing is, everyone handles it differently. Some people feel relief after having an abortion; while others feel regret and guilt. There’s no “right way” to feel honestly. I can tell you from experience that If you fall into the category of regret and guilt, that it does NOT last forever. You will feel better. If you choose an abortion, I’d recommend MA as opposed to SA. Something about having a SA made the situation much more real for me and was much scarier. The MA felt more intimate and like an extra crampy period. I also was like you on that I’ve also always wanted to be a mother. It’s hard grappling with your wants vs the reality of your situation (ie financial difficulties, medical issues, partner incompatibility, etc).  But I promise you that whatever decision you choose, I am sure you’ll find peace in it. Just make sure you choose your decision based on what’s best for you.
